title: Call Directory extension
summary: Expand rules into iOS's block list, incrementally
description:
CURRENT STATE: nothing built. API verified by reading iOS SDK 26.2 headers on the dev machine.

Implement CXCallDirectoryProvider. On beginRequestWithExtensionContext: ask F002 to expand the user's rules and stream the result.

HARD API CONSTRAINTS (from the headers, not documentation):
- addBlockingEntryWithNextSequentialPhoneNumber: takes CXCallDirectoryPhoneNumber (int64_t) and requires STRICTLY ASCENDING order. Out of order fails the whole request. Assert monotonicity in debug.
- No allow list exists. Allow-exceptions are handled in F002 by not emitting the number.
- addIdentificationEntryWithNextSequentialPhoneNumber:label: exists for labels but is unused in release 1 — it belongs to R3, deferred.
- completeRequestWithCompletionHandler: reports `expired` when the run ran out of time. Treat that as a real failure mode, not a warning.

MEMORY AND TIME ARE THE REAL LIMITS: Apple's guidance is to load a subset at a time under autorelease pools. Never materialise the full list. The entry ceiling is F001's measured value, injected as configuration, never a constant.

USE INCREMENTAL UPDATES: isIncremental, removeBlockingEntryWithPhoneNumber:, removeAllBlockingEntries (iOS 11+). Rule edits and dataset updates should push deltas rather than rebuild millions of entries. Handle isIncremental returning NO by rebuilding fully.

TRIGGERING: CXCallDirectoryManager reloadExtensionWithIdentifier: is called by the app after a rule change or a dataset update (F003).

SHARING WITH THE APP: rules and datasets reach the extension through an App Group. The extension cannot assume the app is running.

WHAT THIS EXTENSION CANNOT DO, and the UI must not imply otherwise: it gets no callback when a call is blocked, cannot see call history, and has no control over what the user sees. It is write-only and silent.
